question: If Pristine were to acquire an indian company that had turnover of 1Cr and no assets, would it have to notify the deal to the CCI?
answer_found: Based on the Target Exemption and the Competition (Minimum Value of Assets or Turnover) Rules, 2024, an acquisition is exempt from notification to the CCI if the target company's assets in India are not more than INR 4.5 billion OR its turnover in India is not more than INR 12.5 billion. Since the Indian company has no assets and a turnover of 1 Crore INR (0.01 billion INR), both values are well below the specified thresholds. Therefore, the acquisition would not amount to a combination under section 5 of the Act, and Pristine would not have to notify the deal to the CCI.

Determine if a target company with a turnover of 1 Crore INR and no assets would trigger notification based on these thresholds or any exemptions.

EXTRACTED PASSAGES:
[CCI Combination Guide.pdf, Page 3] "The Indian Government, exercising its powers under section 54(a) of the Act (Power to exempt) issued a notification exempting transactions in which a target company has assets of the value of not more than INR 4.5 billion in India or turnover of not more than INR 12.5 billion in India, from the filing requirement ("Target Exemption")."
[CCI Combination Guide.pdf, Page 3] "As a consequence of this Target Exemption, an acquisition in which the target company falls below the aforesaid thresholds of assets or turnover in India, does not amount to a combination under section 5 of the Act."
[CCI Combination Guide.pdf, Page 14] "The Competition (Minimum Value of Assets or Turnover) Rules, 2024 crystalize the de-minimis exemption and stipulate that under section 5(e) of the Act (Combination), an acquisition, control, merger or amalgamation does not constitute a combination if the value of the assets or turnover of the enterprise being acquired, taken control of, merged or amalgamated in India is below the following prescribed limits (i) The minimum value of assets for an enterprise will be INR4.5bn. (ii) The minimum value of the turnover for an enterprise will be INR12.5bn."

ATTEMPTED ANSWER:
Based on the "Target Exemption" and the Competition (Minimum Value of Assets or Turnover) Rules, 2024, an acquisition does not constitute a combination and is exempted from the filing requirement if the target company's assets in India are not more than INR 4.5 billion or its turnover in India is not more than INR 12.5 billion. Since the Indian company in question has a turnover of 1 Crore INR (which is 0.01 billion INR) and no assets, both values are well below the specified exemption thresholds (INR 4.5 billion for assets and INR 12.5 billion for turnover). Therefore, Pristine would not have to notify the deal to the CCI.
